root:
Puerto — Rust full-stack DDD framework

Usage: puerto <COMMAND>

Commands:
  nuevo        Scaffold a new Puerto project
  generar      Code generators for existing Puerto projects
  listar       List entities and use cases defined in puerto.toml
  validar      Validate puerto.toml (field types, names, entity consistency)
  completions  Print shell completion script
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version
generar:
Code generators for existing Puerto projects

Usage: puerto generar <COMMAND>

Commands:
  scaffold      Scaffold all DDD layers for a new entity (db and CRUD inferred from puerto.toml)
  caso-de-uso   Add a use case to an existing entity
  evento        Declare a custom domain event of a CRUD entity and regenerate its events.rs
                (projects created with --eventos)
  consumidor    Add a consumer to the worker: an event handler, its tests and its registry entry
                (projects created with --eventos)
  correo        Add a mail: its port, its template implementation and its templates (asunto.txt,
                cuerpo.html, cuerpo.txt). The first one also adds Mailpit and SMTP_URL / MAIL_FROM
                to .env
  bootstrap     Regenerate the wiring (presentacion/cableado,
                presentacion/api/src/generado/bootstrap.rs) from puerto.toml
  migracion     Create a new SQLx migration file
  snippets      Write IDE snippet files (.zed/snippets/rust.json, .vscode/puerto.code-snippets)
  dominio       Scaffold only the domain layer for a new entity (domain-first workflow)
  aplicacion    Scaffold only the application layer for an existing entity
  repositorio   Scaffold only the repository (infrastructure) layer for an existing entity
  presentacion  Scaffold only the presentation layer for an existing entity (regenerates
                bootstrap.rs)
  web           Scaffold only the frontend slice of an existing CRUD entity (web projects;
                regenerates web/src/generado/)
  objeto-valor  Declare a shared value object in puerto.toml (reusable across entities)
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

commands.help:
Scaffold a new Puerto project

Usage: puerto nuevo [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --nombre <NAME>          Project name (skips interactive prompt)
      --db                     Include database support (SQLx + Postgres) (skips interactive prompt)
      --sin-db                 Explicitly skip database support without prompting
      --sin-demo               Skip the Saludo demo entity (creates an empty project)
      --sin-web                Skip the web frontend (`web/`: React + daisyUI on Bun)
      --eventos <EVENTS>       Domain events (needs --db): every write records an event in an
                               outbox, relayed through this transport [possible values: db, kafka]
      --auth <AUTH>            Auth: `oidc` verifies an OpenID Connect provider's tokens (Auth0,
                               Keycloak — Keycloak runs in docker-compose.yml for development);
                               `local` keeps accounts and sessions in the project's database (needs
                               --db) [possible values: oidc, local]
      --destino <DESTINATION>  Directory where the project will be created (defaults to current
                               directory)
  -h, --help                   Print help

Scaffold all DDD layers for a new entity (db and CRUD inferred from puerto.toml)

Usage: puerto generar scaffold [OPTIONS] <NAME> [-- <FIELDS>...]

Arguments:
  <NAME>       Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Producto, LineaPedido)
  [FIELDS]...  Fields after -- separator. Primitives: titulo:String precio:i64! nota:opt:String
               etiquetas:vec:String Value Objects: nombre:Nombre:String edad:Edad:i64
               estado:Estado:enum:Activo/Inactivo apodo:Apodo:opt:String Shared VO (type inferred
               from puerto.toml): email:Email

Options:
      --forzar             Overwrite an already-generated entity, discarding hand-written changes in
                           its files
      --publico <PUBLIC>   Auth projects: use cases whose routes need no token, comma-separated
                           (e.g. listar_productos,obtener_producto). Every other route takes `auth:
                           BearerAuth`
      --rol <ROLE>         Auth projects: a role a route requires, <use_case>=<role>,
                           comma-separated (e.g. crear_producto=admin,borrar_producto=admin) —
                           `#[requiere_rol]` on the handler
      --unico <UNIQUE>     A unique over several fields, comma-separated (e.g.
                           jugador_id,partido_id): one partial unique index in Postgres, checked by
                           the in-memory repository too. Repeatable
      --orden <ORDER>      The order of the list, comma-separated, a `-` for descending (e.g.
                           --orden=-puntos,nombre). Then the newest first
      --privado <PRIVATE>  Auth projects: fields public routes answer only to a caller with a
                           session, comma-separated (e.g. email,telefono). Text fields only
  -h, --help               Print help

Add a use case to an existing entity

Usage: puerto generar caso-de-uso <ENTITY> <ACTION>

Arguments:
  <ENTITY>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Producto)
  <ACTION>  Use case action in snake_case (e.g. publicar_producto)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Declare a shared value object in puerto.toml (reusable across entities)

Usage: puerto generar objeto-valor <NAME> <INNER_TYPE>

Arguments:
  <NAME>        Value object name in PascalCase (e.g. Email, Dinero)
  <INNER_TYPE>  Inner primitive type: String, i64, bool, f64, Uuid, DateTime

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Create a new SQLx migration file

Usage: puerto generar migracion <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Migration name in snake_case (e.g. anadir_stock_a_productos)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Declare a custom domain event of a CRUD entity and regenerate its events.rs (projects created with
--eventos)

Usage: puerto generar evento <ENTITY> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <ENTITY>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Producto)
  <NAME>    Event type in snake_case, past tense (e.g. producto_publicado)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Add a consumer to the worker: an event handler, its tests and its registry entry (projects created
with --eventos)

Usage: puerto generar consumidor --tras <ON> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Consumer name in snake_case (e.g. avisar_producto_nuevo)

Options:
      --tras <ON>  The event types it handles, comma-separated (e.g.
                   producto_creado,producto_publicado)
  -h, --help       Print help

Add a mail: its port, its template implementation and its templates (asunto.txt, cuerpo.html,
cuerpo.txt). The first one also adds Mailpit and SMTP_URL / MAIL_FROM to .env

Usage: puerto generar correo [OPTIONS] <NAME> [-- <FIELDS>...]

Arguments:
  <NAME>       Mail name in snake_case (e.g. bienvenida, pedido_enviado)
  [FIELDS]...  The values its text shows, after --: nombre:String plazas:i64 plan:opt:String.
               Primitives and opt:<type> only; the recipient `para` is always there. None:
               nombre:String

Options:
      --tras <ON>  Projects created with --eventos: the worker sends the mail on these event types,
                   comma-separated (e.g. cliente_creado). Its fields come from the events' snapshots
      --para <TO>  With --tras: the String field of the snapshot that holds the recipient (e.g.
                   email)
  -h, --help       Print help

Scaffold only the frontend slice of an existing CRUD entity (web projects; regenerates
web/src/generado/)

Usage: puerto generar web [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Producto)

Options:
      --forzar  Overwrite the entity's existing frontend files, discarding hand-written changes
  -h, --help    Print help

Scaffold only the domain layer for a new entity (domain-first workflow)

Usage: puerto generar dominio [OPTIONS] <NAME> [-- <FIELDS>...]

Arguments:
  <NAME>       Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Producto, LineaPedido)
  [FIELDS]...  Fields after -- separator. Same syntax as `generar scaffold`. They are written to
               puerto.toml, so `generar aplicacion/repositorio/presentacion` pick them up

Options:
      --unico <UNIQUE>     A unique over several fields, comma-separated (e.g.
                           jugador_id,partido_id). Repeatable
      --orden <ORDER>      The order of the list, comma-separated, a `-` for descending (e.g.
                           --orden=-puntos,nombre). Then the newest first
      --privado <PRIVATE>  Auth projects: fields public routes answer only to a caller with a
                           session, comma-separated (e.g. email,telefono). Text fields only
  -h, --help               Print help

Scaffold only the application layer for an existing entity

Usage: puerto generar aplicacion <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Producto)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Scaffold only the repository (infrastructure) layer for an existing entity

Usage: puerto generar repositorio <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Producto)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Scaffold only the presentation layer for an existing entity (regenerates bootstrap.rs)

Usage: puerto generar presentacion <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Producto)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Regenerate the wiring (presentacion/cableado, presentacion/api/src/generado/bootstrap.rs) from
puerto.toml

Usage: puerto generar bootstrap [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --permitir-faltantes  Write the file even when puerto.toml declares entities whose code is not
                            on disk
  -h, --help                Print help

Write IDE snippet files (.zed/snippets/rust.json, .vscode/puerto.code-snippets)

Usage: puerto generar snippets [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --ide <IDE>  Target IDE: zed or vscode (default: both)
  -h, --help       Print help

List entities and use cases defined in puerto.toml

Usage: puerto listar

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Validate puerto.toml (field types, names, entity consistency)

Usage: puerto validar

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Print shell completion script

Usage: puerto completions <SHELL>

Arguments:
  <SHELL>  Shell to generate completions for (bash, zsh, fish, powershell) [possible values: bash,
           elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
